liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Sugaree** (2 reviews): Probably the most powerful performance heard, matching Dicks Picks Vol. 3; Performance gives chills and is definitely amongst the best heard [17][20]
- **Peggy O** (2 reviews): Listener considers this the best version of the song they know; Listener has loved this version since finding an old tape ten years ago [14][16]
- **Scarlet Begonias** (2 reviews): An epic solo over two minutes long cooks in this jam; Jam from Scarlet to Fire is described as just nasty [13][17]
- **Supplication** (1 review): Bobby's vocal performance on this song is described as killer [19]
- **The Music Never Stopped** (1 review): First set closed with a hot performance of this song [12]
- **St. Stephen** (1 review): Performance does not hold a candle to other 1977 versions [18]
- **Johnny B. Goode** (1 review): Garcia shows complete mastery of Chuck Berry licks in this song [22]

## The recordings

- **gd1977-05-05.sbd.unknown.261.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 20 songs; 175 min; rated 3/5 by 3 [1]
- **gd77-05-05.sbd.stephens.8832.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 19 songs; 180 min; rated 4.75/5 by 77 [2]. Said about its sound: Recording quality is delicious and sounds great on iPod, car, and stereo [20]
- **gd1977-05-05.sbd.cantor.7725.shnf**: soundboard; 19 songs; 173 min; rated 4.85/5 by 13 [3]
- **gd1977-05-05.171014.mtx.dusborne.flac1644**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 19 songs; 181 min; rated 3.25/5 by 4 [5]
- **gd1977-05-05.148735.SBD.Betty.Anon.Noel.t-flac2448**: soundboard; 19 songs; 181 min [6]

## Around the show

- Playing was tight and emotional despite rare varied setlists in 1977 [15]
- Second set followed traditional form and really smoked compared to the first [12]
- Show is good but overshadowed by its neighborhood performances [13]
- Show is as good as any May 1977 performance [14]
- Peggy-O solo lacks the emotion and skill of the May 9th version [15]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1977-05-05.sbd.unknown.261.shnf**: transferred by Unknown; source: Soundboard [1]
- **gd77-05-05.sbd.stephens.8832.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [2]
- **gd1977-05-05.sbd.cantor.7725.shnf**: transferred by Troy Wallwork; source: master reels > dat [3]. Also: Other transfers exist and are tracked differently with specific time drops [3]
- **gd1977-05-05.171014.mtx.dusborne.flac1644**: source: 2 Source Matrix by dusborne [5]. Also: Charlie Miller worked on SBD and AUD; Rob Eaton and Dan Stephens on SBD; Doug Lamarre provided AUD cassettes; Scott Clugston worked on the AUD [5]
- **gd1977-05-05.148735.SBD.Betty.Anon.Noel.t-flac2448**: taped by Betty Cantor; transferred by Source & Transfer by Anonymous;Edited & Mastered using Adobe Audition by Joe Noel; source: Source: Betty Cantor's SBD Reel Master > PCM > Beta PCM clone > cloned to wav file on computer by Sony SLHF300 Betamax and modified Sony PCM601esd via spdif… [6]. Also: Anonymous shared the source; Pete Ebel transferred the unknown aud recording [6]

## Art and photos

- Poster by thecurtainwithblog.blogspot.com: [Grateful Dead - 1977-05-05 Veterans Memorial Coliseum, New Haven, CT](https://thecurtainwithblog.blogspot.com/2018/07/grateful-dead-1977-05-05-veterans.html) [24]

- Poster by RareVinyl.com: [Grateful Dead Veterans Memorial Coliseum, New Haven CT 1977 - RSD BF 2024 - 180 Gram Vinyl - EX UK Vinyl box set](https://us.rarevinyl.com/products/grateful-dead-veterans-memorial-coliseum-new-haven-ct-1977-rsd-bf-2024-180-gram-vinyl-ex-uk-vinyl-box-set-603497824694-878352) [27]
